column2: Her canniness with money let the family weather three lean winters.
column3: 她在理財上的精明，讓全家撐過了三個艱困的冬天。
column4: financial canniness (理財上的精明)
column5: can 能 + ny：能精打細算的老狐狸，每一步都先想好

column2: His obtuseness frustrated the teacher, who had explained the joke three times.
column3: 他的遲鈍讓老師很挫折，因為這個笑話她已經解釋了三次。
column4: sheer obtuseness (十足的遲鈍)
column5: obtuse 是鈍角，不尖也不利，腦筋也轉不過來

column2: The politician's vacuous speech was full of slogans but offered no actual plan.
column3: 那位政客的空洞演說充滿口號，卻沒有任何實際計畫。
column4: a vacuous smile (茫然的微笑)
column5: vacuum 是真空，裡面什麼都沒有

column2: It was fatuous to expect applause for such a careless, self-satisfied performance.
column3: 對一場草率又自我感覺良好的表演期待掌聲，實在愚昧可笑。
column4: a fatuous remark (荒唐的言論)
column5: 頭戴皇冠的稻草人，愚昧卻洋洋得意

column2: He posted an inane comment about the weather in the middle of the serious debate.
column3: 在嚴肅的辯論進行時，他發表了一則關於天氣的無聊留言。
column4: an inane remark (空洞的話)
column5: inane 拉丁文原指「空的」，像一個空罐子叮噹響

column2: Credulous tourists believed the guide's claim that the old bridge was magic.
column3: 輕信的遊客相信導遊所說那座老橋有魔法。
column4: a credulous audience (輕信的觀眾)
column5: cred 相信，像 credit card 信用卡，信得太容易

column2: Gullible shoppers believed the ad's promise of a free car with every purchase.
column3: 容易受騙的顧客相信廣告所說每買一件就送一輛車。
column4: too gullible to doubt (輕信到不懷疑)
column5: 魚看到咕嚕咕嚕冒泡的魚餌，一口就上鉤

column2: Scientists remained skeptical of the claim until other labs repeated the experiment.
column3: 在其他實驗室重複這項實驗之前，科學家對此說法仍抱持懷疑。
column4: remain skeptical about (對…持懷疑態度)
column5: 想像瞇著眼睛問「真的嗎？」的人

column2: She gave him an incredulous look when he said he had finished the marathon in an hour.
column3: 當他說自己一小時跑完馬拉松，她投以難以置信的眼神。
column4: an incredulous look (難以置信的表情)
column5: in 不 + cred 相信 → 不肯相信

column2: The dubious contract contained clauses that no honest lawyer would sign.
column3: 那份可疑的合約有些條款，正直的律師絕不會簽。
column4: a dubious claim (可疑的說法)
column5: du 是二：心裡有兩個念頭，半信半疑

column2: Her argument remains tenable because every objection so far has been answered with evidence.
column3: 她的論點依然站得住腳，因為至今每項質疑都已用證據回應。
column4: a tenable position (站得住腳的立場)
column5: ten 是握住：論點被牢牢抓住，不會倒

column2: After the leaked emails appeared, the minister's position became untenable and he resigned.
column3: 外洩的電子郵件曝光後，部長的處境已無法維持，他便辭職了。
column4: an untenable position (站不住腳的立場)
column5: un 不 + tenable：想握也握不住，會滑掉

column2: Her excuse sounded plausible, but the receipts told a different story.
column3: 她的藉口聽起來合情合理，但收據卻說出了另一個版本。
column4: a plausible explanation (合理的解釋)
column5: plaus 是鼓掌：聽起來值得拍手的好理由
column8: 看似合情合理；說得通的

column2: The film's ending is implausible; nobody could survive such a fall unharmed.
column3: 這部電影的結局難以令人信服；沒人能毫髮無傷地從那麼高摔下來。
column4: an implausible story (不可信的故事)
column5: im 不 + plausible：聽了不想鼓掌的說法

column2: Fingerprints on the vase were incontrovertible proof that he had been in the room.
column3: 花瓶上的指紋是他曾在房間裡的確鑿證據。
column4: incontrovertible evidence (無可爭議的證據)
column5: contra 相反 + vert 轉：沒有辦法轉到對面反駁
column7: in - con - tro - vert - i - ble

column2: It is an indisputable fact that water boils at a lower temperature on mountaintops.
column3: 水在山頂上沸點較低，這是無可爭辯的事實。
column4: an indisputable fact (不爭的事實)
column5: in 不 + dispute 爭論 → 沒有人能和它吵架

column2: The video footage provided irrefutable evidence of where the car had been parked.
column3: 影片畫面提供了無可辯駁的證據，顯示那輛車停在何處。
column4: irrefutable proof (無可辯駁的證據)
column5: ir 不 + refute 駁倒 → 怎麼駁都駁不倒

column2: The wildlife sanctuary protects injured owls until they can fly again.
column3: 這座野生動物保護區保護受傷的貓頭鷹，直到牠們能再次飛翔。
column4: a wildlife sanctuary (野生動物保護區)
column5: sanct 是神聖，聖殿裡沒人敢傷害你

column2: The journalist applied for asylum after threats forced her to leave her country.
column3: 在受到威脅被迫離開祖國後，這名記者申請政治庇護。
column4: seek political asylum (尋求政治庇護)
column5: 想像逃到別的國家敲門說「請保護我」
column8: 政治庇護；庇護所；精神病院

column2: The quiet café became a haven for students escaping the noisy dormitory.
column3: 這間安靜的咖啡館成為逃離吵鬧宿舍的學生們的避風港。
column4: a safe haven (安全的避風港)
column5: haven 長得像 heaven：像天堂一樣安全的地方

column2: Families took refuge in the church while the floodwaters rose outside.
column3: 洪水在外頭上漲時，家家戶戶躲進教堂避難。
column4: take refuge in (躲進…避難)
column5: re 回 + fuge 逃，像 fugitive 逃犯：逃回安全的地方

column2: The town's resilience was clear in how quickly shops reopened after the storm.
column3: 風暴過後商店多快重新開張，顯示出這座城鎮的復原力。
column4: show great resilience (展現強大韌性)
column5: re 回 + sil 跳 → 被壓扁後彈跳回來

column2: Children are often resilient, bouncing back quickly from small disappointments.
column3: 孩子通常很有韌性，能從小小的失望中迅速恢復。
column4: remain resilient (保持韌性)
column5: re 回 + sil 跳，像彈簧球被壓下去又彈回來
column8: 有韌性；迅速恢復；適應的

column2: A confirmed misanthrope, he avoided parties and spoke to neighbors only when forced.
column3: 他是個徹底的厭世者，不去派對，只有被迫時才和鄰居說話。
column4: a bitter misanthrope (憤世嫉俗的人)
column5: mis 討厭 + anthrop 人類 → 討厭人群的人

column2: The philanthropist donated millions to build libraries in rural villages.
column3: 這位慈善家捐出數百萬，在鄉下村莊興建圖書館。
column4: a generous philanthropist (慷慨的慈善家)
column5: phil 愛 + anthrop 人類 → 愛人類的人

column2: Her altruism was evident when she gave up her weekends to tutor struggling students.
column3: 她犧牲週末輔導學習吃力的學生，展現出她的無私。
column4: act out of altruism (出於利他而行動)
column5: alter 其他的 → 先替別人著想

column2: A benevolent neighbor shoveled snow from every driveway on the street.
column3: 一位樂善好施的鄰居把街上每戶車道的雪都鏟乾淨。
column4: a benevolent ruler (仁慈的統治者)
column5: bene 好 + vol 意願 → 心懷好意

column2: The villain's malevolent smile showed that he enjoyed other people's misfortune.
column3: 反派的惡毒笑容顯示他樂於看見別人倒楣。
column4: a malevolent glare (惡毒的瞪視)
column5: mal 壞 + vol 意願 → 心懷壞意

column2: Spiteful gossip spread through the office after she won the promotion.
column3: 她獲得升遷後，帶著惡意的八卦在辦公室傳開。
column4: a spiteful remark (惡意的言論)
column5: spite 像 spike 尖刺，故意去扎別人

column2: Years after the divorce, rancor still colored every conversation between them.
column3: 離婚多年後，怨恨仍然影響著他們之間的每次交談。
column4: deep-seated rancor (根深蒂固的怨恨)
column5: rancor 像 rancid 發酸的：放太久而酸臭的怨氣

column2: Centuries of enmity between the two clans made even trade impossible.
column3: 兩個家族數百年的敵意，使得連貿易都不可能。
column4: deep enmity between (之間的深仇)
column5: enmity 就是 enemy 的名詞：變成敵人的狀態

column2: She felt an instant antipathy toward the smug, boastful stranger.
column3: 她對那個自滿又愛吹噓的陌生人立刻產生反感。
column4: feel antipathy toward (對…感到反感)
column5: anti 反 + path 感覺 → 感覺全部往反方向

column2: He has a strong aversion to crowds and avoids shopping malls.
column3: 他極度討厭人群，所以避開購物中心。
column4: have an aversion to (對…反感)
column5: a 離開 + vert 轉 → 一看到就轉頭走開

column2: She has a penchant for collecting vintage postcards from every city she visits.
column3: 她特別愛收集每個造訪城市的復古明信片。
column4: a penchant for adventure (對冒險的偏好)
column5: 法文 pencher 是「傾斜」：心整個傾向某樣東西

column2: The chef's predilection for bold spices shaped every dish on the menu.
column3: 主廚偏愛大膽的香料，影響了菜單上的每一道菜。
column4: a predilection for sweets (偏愛甜食)
column5: pre 先 + dilect 愛 → 在別人之前先愛上

column2: He has a proclivity for procrastination, always leaving homework until midnight.
column3: 他有拖延的習性，總是把作業留到半夜才寫。
column4: a proclivity for risk (冒險的傾向)
column5: pro 向前 + cliv 斜坡 → 站在斜坡上，自然往下滑的傾向

column2: Some dogs have a propensity to bark at any unfamiliar sound.
column3: 有些狗天生傾向對任何陌生聲音吠叫。
column4: a propensity for violence (暴力傾向)
column5: pro 向前 + pens 懸掛 → 身體不自覺向前傾

column2: She felt a natural affinity with the shy new student, having been one herself.
column3: 她自己也曾是新生，所以對那位害羞的轉學生有天然的親近感。
column4: an affinity for music (與音樂的親近感)
column5: af 向 + fin 邊界 → 住在隔壁邊界，自然很親近
column8: 親近感；雷同；吸引力；密切關係

column2: The autonomous region manages its own schools while following national defense policy.
column3: 這個自治區自行管理學校，同時遵循國家的國防政策。
column4: an autonomous region (自治區)
column5: auto 自己 + nomos 法律 → 自己定規矩

column2: Employees given greater autonomy often feel more responsible for the results of their work.
column3: 獲得更多自主權的員工，往往對工作成果更有責任感。
column4: gain greater autonomy (獲得更大自主權)
column5: auto 自己 + nomy 管理 → 自己管自己
